expected_approaches.summary: Return immediately when a value has already been observed in a hash set.
expected_approaches.applicability: Unordered values when expected linear time is desired.
key_invariants: The set contains exactly the values examined so far.
tradeoffs: Uses memory proportional to distinct input values.
common_failure_modes: checking membership after an unconditional insert

alternative_approaches.summary: Sort the values, either in place or in a copy, and compare neighboring values.
alternative_approaches.applicability: When sorting is acceptable and hashing is undesirable.
assumptions: Mutating input is either allowed or a copy is made.
key_invariants: Equal values become adjacent after sorting.
alternative_approaches.space_complexity: O(1) auxiliary only for an in-place constant-space sort; O(n) for an input copy, with additional working storage depending on the sorting implementation
tradeoffs: An in-place sort changes input order; preserving the input requires a copy and O(n) additional storage.

reference_solutions.source_code: class Solution { public: bool containsDuplicate(vector<int> nums) { unordered_set<int> seen; for(int value: nums) if(!seen.insert(value).second) return true; return false; } };
class Solution { public boolean containsDuplicate(int[] nums) { java.util.Set<Integer> seen=new java.util.HashSet<>(); for(int value:nums) if(!seen.add(value)) return true; return false; } }

invariants.diagnostic_goal: The set is the distinct-value summary of the inspected prefix.

complexity_expectations.diagnostic_goal: Explain expected O(n) work when the full array is scanned, possible early exit, and the lack of a universal worst-case hash guarantee.

common_misconceptions.diagnostic_goal: Recognize that the set can grow with the input.

failure_modes.diagnostic_goal: Check whether insertion was new before continuing.

edge_cases.diagnostic_goal: Return false when no pair can exist.
Do not rely on adjacent input values.

counterexamples.purpose: A duplicate far apart defeats adjacent-only scanning.
A single value is never duplicated.

constraint_mutations.diagnostic_goal: Compare a sort-based approach when hash-set memory is constrained.

probe_opportunities.diagnostic_goal: Defend why a repeated value is detected exactly when it is encountered again.
Compare sort-and-scan with a hash set.

weak_or_misconception_signals: cannot explain why distant duplicates work
sample_phrasings: What does the set represent after each iteration?

common_followups.diagnostic_goal: Test space accounting for distinct values.
weak_or_misconception_signals: treats a growing set as constant
sample_phrasings: How large can the set become when no duplicate appears?

common_followups.diagnostic_goal: Test why sorting makes equality local.
expected_good_signals: equal values are adjacent after sorting
sample_phrasings: Why is one adjacent scan enough after sorting?

level_considerations.guidance: Assess whether the candidate can choose and use a set correctly.
Expect explicit time and space tradeoff reasoning.

reference_reasoning: A hash set is the reviewed expected approach, while sorting and other plausible correct strategies remain valid when their tradeoffs are defended.
